intro: Match each skill line to what it actually asks you to do.

left.label: HC — Historical Context
hints: Think about what comes BEFORE you make your argument.
It's the move that sets the scene — time, place, circumstances — not the argument itself.

left.label: TH — Thesis
hints: This is about taking a side, not describing one.
A clear position you can actually argue for or against.

left.label: DU — Document Use
hints: This is about USING a document, not just mentioning it exists.
Name a specific detail from the document and use it as evidence.

left.label: EX — Explanation
hints: This is the 'so what' move — why does the evidence matter?
If your sentence doesn't say WHY the evidence proves your point, this skill isn't happening yet.

left.label: OE — Outside Evidence
hints: This is knowledge from outside the documents you were given.
The exam's own term for this is 'outside information.'

left.label: CP — Civic Principle
hints: This means saying the actual name of a principle, not just describing it.
"Federalism" or "equal protection" said out loud — not just implied.

right.label: Warm up the document — set the scene before you argue
Take a clear position and hold it. Try: “Although ___, ___ because ___.”
Name the document. Pull a specific detail. Use it as evidence — don't just point at it
The “so what.” After every piece of evidence, say why it matters
Bring in something NOT in the documents — a law, case, or event
Name it out loud — equal protection, federalism, checks and balances. Don't imply it

rationale.a: Historical Context sets the scene — the circumstances around the document — before you make an argument.
rationale.b: Thesis is a clear, held position, not just a topic.
rationale.c: Document Use means naming a specific detail from a document and using it as evidence, not just gesturing at the source.
rationale.d: Explanation is the "so what" — why the evidence matters, not just that it exists.
rationale.e: Outside Evidence is knowledge from beyond the documents themselves — what the exam calls "outside information."
rationale.f: Civic Principle has to be named out loud ("federalism," "equal protection") — implying it isn't enough.

_hint_model: 2 escalating hints per pair, available during the regular season only. Playoffs run cold (no hints), per BK's ruling 2026-09-22.
